findings.title: df2mat uses deprecated select_dtypes(include=['object']): Pandas4Warning on every categorical-DataFrame plot (e.g. mushrooms demo)
findings.description: hypertools/tools/df2mat.py:31-32 calls data.select_dtypes(include=['object']) / exclude=['object'] to split text columns. Under pandas 3.0.3 (str dtype era) this relies on deprecated back-compat and emits a Pandas4Warning on the flagship categorical workflow hyp.plot(hyp.load('mushrooms')). When pandas removes the back-compat, str-dtype columns will no longer match 'object': df_str becomes empty, the raw str columns stay in df_num, and df_num.values becomes an object array that downstream np.isnan/reducers cannot handle (per the code's own comment) - i.e. the categorical->dummies expansion silently breaks. This is our own code path hitting a pandas API change, which the release bar treats as major.
findings.repro: env MPLBACKEND=Agg PYTHONWARNINGS=always /Users/jmanning/hypertools/.venv/bin/python -c "import hypertools as hyp; m = hyp.load('mushrooms'); fig = hyp.plot(m, '.')"
findings.expected: No deprecation warnings from hypertools code on a documented example dataset; select_dtypes call future-proofed (e.g. include=['object','str'] or dtype-kind based selection).
findings.actual: /Users/jmanning/hypertools/hypertools/tools/df2mat.py:32: Pandas4Warning: For backward compatibility, 'str' dtypes are included by select_dtypes when 'object' dtype is specified. This behavior is deprecated and will be removed in a future version. Explicitly pass 'str' to `include` to select them, or to `exclude` to remove them and silence this warning.

findings.title: Core dependency pydata-wrangler passes deprecated copy= to pd.concat: Pandas4Warning on multi-dataset manip/normalize, future hard break
findings.description: hyp.manip([a, b], 'ZScore') (any multi-dataset funnel/unfunnel path through datawrangler) emits Pandas4Warning from datawrangler/decorate/decorate.py:421, which calls pd.concat(..., copy=...). pandas 3 deprecated the copy keyword; when removed, this pd.concat call raises TypeError and core hypertools list-input paths break. Appears 6x in tests/test_manip_impute_hardening.py alone. The fix belongs upstream in pydata-wrangler (same maintainers) or via a pandas pin; either way hypertools 1.0 users on pandas 3 currently see a deprecation warning from a plain 2-dataset z-score.

findings.actual: /Users/jmanning/hypertools/.venv/lib/python3.12/site-packages/datawrangler/decorate/decorate.py:421: Pandas4Warning: The copy keyword is deprecated and will be removed in a future version. findings.title: Legacy {'params'} cluster/reduce dict DeprecationWarning is invisible on the plot()/analyze() paths (stacklevel lands in library frames)
findings.description: The DeprecationWarning for the legacy {'model','params'} spec uses stacklevel=3, which is correct for direct hyp.cluster()/hyp.reduce() calls (warning attributed to user code, visible under default filters in __main__). But through hyp.plot() or hyp.analyze() the 3-frame offset lands inside hypertools (observed attributions: plot/backend.py:1182, plot/plot.py:1756, tools/analyze.py:192). Because Python's default filters only display DeprecationWarning when it is attributed to __main__, a user calling hyp.plot(d, cluster={'model':'KMeans','params':{...}}) sees NOTHING (verified: empty stderr under default filters), so the deprecation cannot steer plot() users to migrate before the legacy form is removed.

findings.title: 44/59 warnings.warn calls set no stacklevel and no category (bare UserWarning pointing at library internals); 15 do - inconsistent
findings.description: AST census over hypertools/ (excluding _externals): 59 warnings.warn call sites; only 15 pass stacklevel and only 15 pass an explicit category. The other 44 emit bare UserWarnings attributed to hypertools's own file/line, so (a) users cannot locate which of their calls triggered the warning, (b) warnings.filterwarnings(module=...) targeting user modules cannot match, and (c) there is no hypertools-specific warning class to filter selectively. sklearn/pandas convention is stacklevel>=2 plus dedicated categories. The codebase is inconsistent with itself (e.g. sources.py and cluster.py do it right).
findings.expected: Consistent stacklevel pointing at user code and a hypertools warning category (or at least uniform practice).
findings.actual: total warn calls: 59; with stacklevel: 15; with explicit category: 15

findings.title: plotly backend auto-show in plain scripts leaks a socket (ResourceWarning) and launches a browser; show=False is clean
findings.description: With the plotly backend, hyp.plot() in a non-interactive script deliberately calls fig.show() (documented design in plotly_backend.py:983-993), which routes through plotly's open_html_in_browser: it spins up a localhost HTTP server socket and opens the user's browser. plotly never closes the socket, so any warnings-enabled run (pytest, -W always, PYTHONDEVMODE) prints a ResourceWarning. A batch script producing N figures opens N browser tabs + N leaked sockets. The root leak is upstream (plotly _base_renderers.py:717) but hypertools's auto-show triggers it; verified that show=False produces no socket/warning. Consider documenting show=False prominently for scripted use or using a file-based renderer for headless contexts.

findings.title: Discarded/rebound animate results trigger matplotlib 'Animation was deleted without rendering anything' - 41 occurrences in hypertools's own animation test files
findings.description: hyp.plot(d, animate=True) returns a HyperAnimation; if the result is unbound, del'd, or rebound in a loop before saving/rendering (common exploratory pattern), matplotlib warns at GC with guidance ('use plt.show() or anim.save()') that does not mention hypertools's own idiom (save_path=). The suite sample shows this is the dominant source of the reported ~304 test-suite warnings: 41 of 52 warnings across tests/test_animation_styles.py (11), tests/test_hyper_animation.py (10), tests/test_window_animation.py (20). Holding the object until interpreter exit does NOT warn (verified). Fix options: render/close in tests, or have HyperAnimation absorb the matplotlib warning and re-emit actionable hypertools guidance.
findings.repro: env MPLBACKEND=Agg PYTHONWARNINGS=always /Users/jmanning/hypertools/.venv/bin/python -c "import gc, numpy as np; import hypertools as hyp; d=np.cumsum(np.random.randn(60,4),axis=0); ani=hyp.plot(d, animate=True, duration=1, frame_rate=8); del ani; gc.collect()"
findings.expected: Either no warning or a hypertools-idiomatic message (mention save_path=/HyperAnimation.save); test suite should not emit 41 of these.
findings.actual: /Users/jmanning/hypertools/.venv/lib/python3.12/site-packages/matplotlib/animation.py:908: UserWarning: Animation was deleted without rendering anything. This is most likely not intended. To prevent deletion, assign the Animation to a variable, e.g. `anim`, that exists until you output the Animation using `plt.show()` or `anim.save()`.

findings.title: Warning-classification table for release notes: upstream import-time warning-filter mutations are NOT hypertools's doing (documented here as proof of triage)
findings.description: Classification of every remaining unique warning/global-state effect observed across all runs, with attribution: (1) scipy adds 3 'ignore' filters (ndarray/ufunc/dtype size changed) + RankWarning 'always' at import - upstream, unavoidable, affects every scipy user; (2) sklearn adds SpecialFunctionWarning 'always' + a case-insensitive 'ignore' for 'the matrix subclass is not the recommended way' - upstream (any sklearn import), means users won't see numpy matrix-subclass PendingDeprecationWarnings after importing hypertools; (3) requests/urllib3 add 4 filters - upstream; (4) first hyp.plot() imports IPython for frontend detection, which installs an 'error' filter for IPython.core.completer.ProvisionalCompleterWarning - upstream IPython behavior, negligible impact; (5) umap n_jobs-overridden-by-random_state UserWarning when users pass n_jobs+random_state - upstream, correct; (6) sklearn SpectralEmbedding 'Graph is not fully connected' - upstream, data-dependent, informative; (7) PPCA missing-data warnings (format_data.py:236, external/ppca.py:154, impute/ppca.py:52) - hypertools's own, deliberately informative, GOOD messages (ppca.py:52 even names the alternative model and GH issue). hypertools itself installs zero global filters and leaves np.geterr() untouched (verified). No deprecated numpy/pandas/matplotlib API usage found in hypertools source by grep; the only dependency-API-change exposures are findings 001-004.
findings.repro: See tested cases 'global state' and 'filters bisect': python -c "import warnings; b=list(warnings.filters); import sklearn; print([f for f in warnings.filters if f not in b])"
findings.actual: hypertools adds 0 filters; scipy 4, sklearn 2, requests/urllib3 4, IPython 1 (on first plot).

findings.title: Public functions shadow their subpackages: 'import hypertools.plot.backend as B' fails with cryptic ImportError "cannot import name 'backend' from 'plot' (unknown location)"
findings.description: hypertools/__init__.py binds the package attributes hypertools.plot, hypertools.reduce, hypertools.cluster, hypertools.align, etc. to FUNCTIONS (from .plot.plot import plot ...), shadowing the identically-named subpackages. Plain 'import hypertools.plot.backend' and 'from hypertools.plot import backend' both work (sys.modules holds the real module), but the equally-idiomatic 'import hypertools.plot.backend as B' resolves the dotted chain via attribute lookup, hits the plot FUNCTION, and dies with ImportError: cannot import name 'backend' from 'plot' (unknown location) - a message that names a bare module 'plot' that the user never imported and gives no hint that hypertools.plot is a function or that 'from hypertools.plot import backend' works. The function-as-attribute design is intentional and long-standing (users call hyp.plot(...)), so this is filed as an error-message/API rough edge rather than a bug; a release-notes or FAQ line ('to reach submodules use from hypertools.plot import ...') would cover it.
findings.expected: Either the import works, or the error explains that hypertools.plot is the plot() function and suggests 'from hypertools.plot import backend'.
findings.actual: ImportError: cannot import name 'backend' from 'plot' (unknown location)  [verified same session: 'import hypertools.plot.backend' -> OK; 'from hypertools.plot import backend' -> OK, BACKEND_WARNING=None; type(hypertools.plot) is function]
